harnessLoss: The first Appearance capture compared renderer-specific section text, so Web controls and truthful Lynx unavailable status copy produced a false content mismatch.
The first workbench fallback identified Lynx as Nightly while the production Web fallback was Alpha, exposing an extra Environment identification row and invalidating the capture identity.
The old row geometry reader depended on the Lynx-only settings-row class and returned no per-row Web measurements.
intentionalPlatformDelta: Web Glass opacity and Word wrap controls are available; Lynx truthfully exposes those rows as unavailable with aria-disabled=true, data-settings-unavailable=true, status copy, and opacity 0.48.
The unavailable status line increases the Lynx Appearance panel from 271.375px to 350px. This height is required explanatory content, not a geometry defect.
Environment identification is hidden in both Alpha renderers and is therefore absent from this cell.
classification.evidenceBoundary: The retained Browser cell uses one immutable snapshot, route, dark theme, 1280x820 viewport, Alpha branding, and zero-error console. It proves shared row content and geometry plus explicit unavailable semantics. It does not claim that unavailable controls should match Web controls, does not remove their explanatory height, and does not claim current dark Native parity.
